title: Product
description: One product of a venture, stored as a card at products/<id>.json (EE-011). It holds the product's own market, job, technology, offering and business model; Product Anatomy judges it against the venture's core and assigns its portfolio role per phase.

market.description: Who is served (Abell: customer groups). One market, or several with one marked primary.

relationship.description: How the people in this market stand to the product (EE-021): customer buys, client is served under a professional relationship, user uses (may not pay), member belongs, audience reads, watches or listens, partner works with the venture

vertical.description: true: one industry; false: across many (horizontal)
true: one industry; false: across many (horizontal)

primary.description: The market the product is mainly built for; exactly one when several are listed

job.description: The need it meets (Abell: customer function; jobs to be done)

technology.description: How it meets the need (Abell: alternative technologies)

ai.description: What AI is to the product. feature: the product works without the model. ai-harness: the product is the software around a model (a chatbot); remove the model and nothing is left. agent-harness: an AI harness where the model directs its own steps and tool use toward a goal. Tests in docs/ontology.md.

scope.description: Where in the system the product works: the whole system, one layer, or one tier of the operations layer. Kits use it most (a knowledge-layer kit, a delivery-tier kit).

part_of.description: Kits this product is bundled into, by product id in the same venture. A part can still be its own product with its own market and portfolio role.

business_model.description: Pattern ids from schema/vocab/business-models.json: the St. Gallen Business Model Navigator's 55 (subscription, freemium, add-on and so on) plus named extras such as open-core

allowed_from.description: The first phase in which it may lead (a standing decision can hold a product back)

flows_to.description: Products this one sends users, data or revenue to; Product Anatomy computes spillover from these

software.description: The product is, or contains, software the venture builds. Such a product needs a repository, so its venture (or a parent) lists one in repos (EE-020)

repo.description: The id of the repository in the venture's (or a parent's) repos that holds its code

offered_to.description: The ICP profiles (purpose/icp.json ids) the product is offered to: who buys or adopts it, and so whom its marketing addresses first (EE-064). In a B2B2C or partner-led venture these are the partners, not the partners' customers.

features.description: What the product does. Each feature names the job it serves: a job of an ICP profile in offered_to. The jobs stay on the ICP record and are read by id, not copied here.

job.description: The job this feature serves. It must be a job of an ICP profile this product is offered to.

serves.description: ICP profiles the product ultimately serves through those it is offered to, such as a partner's own customers (EE-064)
